objective_for_doctor: A 18-year-old Male patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have lower chest pain, bouts of choking or shortness of breath that wake you up at night, and swelling in one or more areas of your body.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi doctor. I have lower chest pain, and I get bouts of choking or shortness of breath that wake me up at night. I also have swelling in my legs—my left ankle and both calves/tibias—and I feel short of breath with activity and when I lie flat.

Doctor: Thanks—these symptoms sound concerning for a breathing/circulation problem (possibly fluid in the lungs or heart/lung blockage). When you wake up choking, do you also have chest pressure or palpitations, and have you had fever or cough?

I don’t have fever or a cough that I can say for sure. When I wake up choking, I also feel my chest pain/pressure, and I get really short of breath—I'm not sure about palpitations, but the breathing feels like it cuts off.

Doctor: Thank you—nighttime choking with chest pressure and shortness of breath plus leg swelling and worse breathing when lying flat strongly suggests heart-related fluid overload. Do you have any history of blood clots, recent long travel/surgery, known heart disease, or do you have one leg that’s more swollen than the other?

I don’t have any recent long travel. I don’t know about blood clots history. My swelling is in the legs on both sides, but it feels worse on the left—like my left ankle is most noticeable. I do have known heart failure.

Doctor: Known heart failure makes this most consistent with worsening fluid overload/heart-failure exacerbation causing pulmonary congestion and orthopnea; to rule out a clot or other acute causes, do you have any new rapid weight gain, and what is your current oxygen level if you’ve checked?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: BNP/NT-proBNP and Basic_Metabolic_Panel (kidney/electrolytes)  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray and ECG

I haven’t checked my oxygen level. I can’t say about rapid weight gain either—I haven’t been weighing myself closely. I do have the shortness of breath that gets worse when I lie flat, and my legs are swelling.

Doctor: Given known heart failure plus orthopnea (worse lying flat), nighttime choking with chest pressure, and bilateral leg swelling, this is very likely an acute heart-failure exacerbation with pulmonary congestion; do you currently have fewer urinations than usual or very high blood pressure?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Troponin and D-dimer (if available) / Venous_Doppler of lower extremities  
Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute decompensated congestive heart failure with volume overload (pulmonary congestion causing orthopnea/paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea)
